name: VoiceOS
description:
VoiceOS is a voice-driven assistant that combines dictation with agent-style actions across the apps and information on your computer. Rather than only transcribing speech at the cursor, it uses the area you point to as context for requests such as finding a file, drafting a message, or creating a follow-up task.

The intended workflow is to press the assigned key, speak a goal, and review the result or action in the relevant app. It can be useful when switching among email, chat, calendars, files, notes, and web research creates more friction than the task itself.

This is a high-permission category of tool. VoiceOS says audio is not stored on its servers or used to train models, while the actions it can take and the data it needs to access still deserve careful review, especially for accounts, files, messages, and external communications.

## Features

- Use dictation mode to turn speech into text and agent mode to request actions rather than only transcription.
- Point at screen context and ask the assistant to locate relevant files, emails, documents, notes, or web results.
- Use supported connections and applications for actions such as drafting or sending email, replying in Slack, scheduling meetings, creating notes, and filing tickets.
- Keep a requested task active so VoiceOS can bring it back at an appropriate time according to its current agent workflow.
- Control whether transcripts are saved on the device and whether anonymous diagnostic or crash reports are shared.
- Rely on the developer’s stated audio policy: audio is not stored on its servers and is not used to train models.

## Where it fits

VoiceOS is for people who want voice input to start or complete multi-app work, not merely dictate text. It may be useful for repetitive communication and retrieval work when the available integrations match the tools you already use.

Treat every external action as something to review before it is sent or committed. It is not a substitute for checking facts, permissions, recipients, or the security of the accounts and files connected to it.
